subject.auditScope: Internal self-audit of AGS v1.5.0 audit/reporting foundation, based on repository evidence and local deterministic examples.

executiveSummary: AGS v1.5.0 demonstrates a working governance spine and a first Governance Reality Report foundation. The self-audit identifies meaningful strengths in proposal scrutiny, action authorization, runtime binding, receipts, red-team and dogfood evals, and audit report generation. It also records watch items where evidence, integration depth, external review, and productized audit workflows remain incomplete.

findings.title: Audit-core adapter coverage is foundational
findings.summary: Runtime Binding exists in AGS, but the audit-core adapter layer is not yet deeply integrated with every package output.
findings.observation: The repository includes Runtime Binding and a lightweight audit adapter foundation. The self-audit does not demonstrate full conversion coverage for every AGS output shape.
findings.whyItMatters: A professional auditor workflow benefits from consistent conversion of runtime, receipt, eval, participation, authority, and gap evidence into report findings.
auditQuestions: Which AGS package outputs are directly convertible into audit findings today?
Which outputs still require manual report authoring or future adapter work?
recommendedRemediations: Expand deterministic adapters package by package, starting with runtime binding, receipts, participation quality, red-team results, and alignment gaps.
Add fixture-backed tests for each supported adapter path.

findings.title: Evidence locker is future work
findings.summary: AGS has receipts and report evidence references, but no dedicated evidence locker is included in v1.5.0.
findings.observation: The self-audit relies on local files and fixtures. It does not include a persistent evidence locker, chain of custody workflow, or third-party evidence review.
findings.whyItMatters: Professional audit workflows need durable evidence references that can be reviewed independently and tied back to report findings.
auditQuestions: Where will evidence artifacts live when reports are prepared for external review?
How will evidence integrity and access be preserved without adding unnecessary data handling?
recommendedRemediations: Design an evidence locker interface before adding storage behavior.
Keep evidence handling local and deterministic until a reviewed storage model exists.

findings.title: Release and package version alignment should be clarified
findings.summary: Repository release version and individual package versions may not align one-to-one.
findings.observation: The release history tracks AGS milestones, while package manifests may retain package-specific versions.
findings.whyItMatters: Clear version labeling helps auditors understand which package artifacts correspond to a release milestone.
auditQuestions: Which package versions correspond to AGS v1.5.0 and v1.5.1?
Should release documentation include a package-version matrix?
recommendedRemediations: Add a release-to-package version note in release documentation.
Avoid implying package version parity unless manifests are intentionally aligned.

findings.title: Public-source review workflow is not yet first-class
findings.summary: The report model supports public-source review mode, but no first-class public-source review workflow is included in v1.5.0.
findings.observation: Examples focus on local fixture inputs. Public-source review workflow mechanics, evidence capture, and agency chain mapping remain future work.
findings.whyItMatters: Public-source review needs clear limitations, evidence capture, and non-accusatory posture so outputs remain professional and verifiable.
auditQuestions: What inputs are acceptable for a public-source review?
How should public claims be separated from verified control evidence?
recommendedRemediations: Create a deterministic public-source review input format.
Add agency chain mapper and evidence reference conventions before external-facing use.

selfAuditDisclosure.scopeDisclosure: This is an internal self-audit of AGS v1.5.0 repository evidence. It is prepared by the project itself and should not be treated as independent external assurance.
strengths: Runtime Binding exists for permit-bound execution.
Receipts exist for proof and accountability.
Red-team and dogfood eval suites exist.
watchItems: Audit-core adapter layer is foundational and not yet deeply integrated with every package output.
Package versions may not align with repo release version.
Public-source review workflow is not yet first-class.
Evidence locker and agency chain mapper are future work.
selfAuditDisclosure.nonCertificationStatement: This self-audit does not claim AGS is enterprise certified, legally compliant, regulator-approved, or production-guaranteed.
